Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior

Interface EyeBehavior

public interface EyeBehavior
One named eye expression (stare, blink, grow, …). Behaviors are stateless singletons registered in EyeBehaviors under a ResourceLocation id; the server names a behavior by id in the trigger packet and the client looks it up to play. All per-play state lives in a BehaviorInstance.

A mob plays at most one behavior at a time (the server enforces this), so behaviors never compose. They participate in the eye physics simulation, not the renderer: once per simulation tick the simulator asks the single active behavior to fill an EyeInfluence per eye — a pupil spring (anchor + stiffness) and/or the non-physical overlays (scale, squash, tint). The renderer then just interpolates and draws the resulting eye state; it never touches behaviors.

Implementations must stay free of client-only imports: the server class-loads this registry to pick and schedule behaviors, and only the client ever calls influence(com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.BehaviorInstance, int, int, com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.EyeInfluence).

  • Method Details

    • influence

      void influence(BehaviorInstance instance, int head, int eye, EyeInfluence out)
      Fill out (already reset) with this eye's influence for the current simulation tick, derived from instance.age. Called per eye, so per-eye behaviors (blink mask, cross-eye target direction) can vary their output by head/eye via instance.helper.
